title: introduce-anticipatory-batch-catalog-and-econ-runner
author: Lena Ortiz
description: Summary: Adds an 'econ-runner' CLI and an anticipatory batch catalog that synthesizes per-tenant batching/caching defaults and candidate quantization profiles based on recent traffic signals and unit-econ targets. Motivation: customers with spiky but predictable patterns (scheduled reports, nightly batch jobs, and periodic tenant ramps) need safer automated defaults for batching, prefetching, and quantization that reduce unit cost without risking tail latency regressions. This PR introduces a production-safe, tenant-aware pipeline that (1) samples recent traffic patterns, (2) simulates batch/cache/quant trade-offs locally using the existing cost simulator, and (3) provisions suggested defaults that can be applied as tenant profiles or validated via canary routes. Design: - econ-runner CLI (Go) orchestrates sampling, local sim, and profile output; supports dry-run and apply modes. - anticipatory_batch_catalog: stores candidate batch sizes, KV cache TTL heuristics, and quant profiles ranked by expected tokens-per-dollar and P95 latency impact. - integration with telemetry: cost signal collector exports a recent window (30d) of token distributions and sequence lengths; runner uses this to seed sims. - runtime adjustments: lightweight admission filter in the scheduler consults tenant profile when routing to prefer compact profiles under cost targets; fallback to standard profile on SLA pressure. Migration and safety: default mode is dry-run. The apply step creates tenant-scoped proposal objects in the control plane (not auto-applied) unless --auto-apply is set and the tenant has opted-in. We added a conservative guard: only profiles with simulated P95 < baseline + 10ms and estimated unit-cost delta > 3% are proposed for apply. Testing and validation: unit tests for sim harness, integration tests against local runtime mock, end-to-end smoke with a synthetic tenant workload, and a benchmark sweep covering small/medium/large sequence lengths. Rollout plan: feature gate behind internal flag; start with opt-in beta tenants; monitor cost delta and latency SLOs; auto-revert if regressions observed. Checklist: - [x] econ-runner CLI and docs - [x] anticipatory batch catalog proto and persistence - [x] simulation harness wiring and test coverage - [x] safe-apply guardrails and opt-in path - [x] console doc and short how-to - [x] perf bench run and telemetry dashboards updated Notes: This PR prioritizes conservative defaults — it is intentionally restrictive to avoid surprise regressions. Future follow-ups: continuous learning loop (automatic proposals after N successful applies), and a UI flow in Console for reviewing proposals.
commits: init econ-runner CLI scaffold; add sampling and cost-sim glue code; implement anticipatory_batch_catalog persistence + API; runtime scheduler admission filter consults tenant profile; add integration and benchmark tests; docs and how-to; tighten guardrails based on reviewer feedback
review_comments: Marcus Nguyen: Please ensure the sim harness uses the same kernel/quant code paths as production. If we diverge we get optimistic cost estimates.
Author (Lena Ortiz): Updated the harness to invoke the runtime kernel selector in 'sim-mode' and added a smoke test that compares sim output to a 1k-sample production replay.
Aria Cho: I think the guard threshold for P95 is tight; can we make it tenant-configurable and default to 10ms? Also add an early-exit if the workload has >80% short sequences (no batching benefit).
Author: Added tenant-configurable guard and early-exit heuristic; documented behaviour in the guide.
Samir Patel: CI flake on the integration suite (random timeout). Suggest increasing test timeout and marking unstable test as flaky with retry.
Author: Added retry wrapper and increased timeout; reran CI.
release_notes: Introduces econ-runner CLI and anticipatory batch catalog. Admins can generate tenant-specific batching, cache, and quantization proposals based on historical signals. Safe-apply requires opt-in; proposals can be reviewed in Console. Expect conservative cost savings (see perf summary).
perf_summary: Simulated tenant sweep: median tokens-per-dollar improvement 4.6% (95% CI 3.2%–6.1%) across synthetic workloads; p95 latency impact median +6ms (guarded under threshold). In closed beta with three tenants, observed actual cost reduction 3.8% with no P95 SLA violations over 72h.
notes_for_oncall: If an applied proposal causes latency spikes, admin can revert tenant profile via control-plane API: DELETE /v1/tenant/{id}/proposals/{proposal_id}. There is an automatic 30-minute monitor that rolls back applied profiles if P95 > baseline + 25ms.
compatibility: Compatible with hosted and Dedicated. Private installations require the telemetry collector to be enabled or the runner to be fed offline token distribution snapshots.
migration_steps: 1) Run econ-runner in dry-run to generate proposals. 2) Review proposals in Console. 3) Apply to opt-in tenants. 4) Monitor dashboards and revert if necessary.
changelog_entry: Added econ-runner CLI and anticipatory batch catalog for tenant-scoped batching/caching/quant proposals (opt-in).
author_acknowledgements: Thanks to Marcus for kernel selector fixes, Aria for guardrail and early-exit heuristics, and SRE for validation guidance.
qa_notes: Run the included integration test with TEST_TENANT_SAMPLE and verify the proposal JSON has expected fields: batch_size, cache_ttl_ms, quant_profile, expected_unit_cost_delta.
ops_notes: Default is dry-run — enabling --auto-apply requires tenant opt-in and setting internal feature flag 'econ.anticipatory.auto_apply' to true.
user_documentation: docs/guide/anticipatory-batching.md contains step-by-step instructions and console screenshots for reviewing proposals.
